newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end down on profit-taking.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended down on Monday on profit-taking and slow trading as many investors took to the sidelines to wait for a clearer direction, traders said.
The most actively traded August 1997 contract ended at 23,540 yuan ($2,837) per tonne, losing 60 yuan. It opened at an intraday high of 23,700 and hit a low of 23,500 yuan per tonne.
May fell 60 yuan to 23,400, June 100 to 23,500, July 60 to 23,540, September 100 to 23,480, October 70 to 23,430 yuan.
Combined volume fell to 17,210 tonnes from 27,190 tonnes.
Copper opened mixed and fell slightly for most of the session.
Traders said many investors were being cautious as a lack of market moving news made it difficult to predict trends.
"Many investors have lost direction and they would rather take profits," one trader said. "But sharp falls are unlikely in the short term due to firm physical prices."
Physical copper prices are around 23,400 yuan per tonne in the Shanghai area.
Traders said the London Metal Exchange would continue to be a major factor on the Shanghai copper in the next few days with no domestic market-moving news in sight.
Aluminium ended down. May fell 180 yuan to 15,400, June 300 to 15,600 and July 340 to 15,750 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume rose to 320 tonnes from 280 tonnes.
